review_notes:
I read all 54 lines of the file and the `matrixOperator` interface it depends on in MatrixAction.lean. That file has `@[simp] matrixOperator_apply`, which is `rfl`. I also looked at every downstream use of `OAI.TwoPointCorrelations.coordinateProjection` under lean/OAI/NumberTheory/TwoPoint, and checked how Mathlib treats similar if-then-else "apply" lemmas (`Finsupp.indicator_apply`, `Set.indicator_apply`/`mulIndicator_apply`, `Matrix.diagonal_apply`).

The file has no simp attributes. Its only rewriting lemma is `coordinateProjection_apply`, and callers pass it to `simp` or `rw` by hand every time. In the two places where `keep i` is false, they also add `ite_eq_right` by hand. That is the one finding.

Other checks:
- Stating `coordinateProjection_idempotent` as `P * P = P` is a reasonable choice, because downstream code (GraphSpectralTransfer) passes it directly as a projection hypothesis. I found no use that needs an applied form `P (P v) = P v`, so I did not report it.
- The `change` to a sum on line 21 could become `rw [coordinateProjection, matrixOperator_apply]`. This is a small proof-style point, not a problem with the simp interface.
- Making `coordinateProjection_apply` simp should not cause a loop: the RHS does not contain `coordinateProjection`, and the existing simp lemma `matrixOperator_apply` cannot fire, because `coordinateProjection` is a plain (non-reducible) definition.
- The `ite` in the RHS uses a classical instance because of `open scoped Classical`. `if_pos` and `if_neg` work with any instance, so this should not hurt users. I could not run Lean to confirm the proposed simp sets close every downstream goal.

findings.excerpt:
lemma coordinateProjection_apply (keep : V → Prop) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ V) (i : V) :
    coordinateProjection keep v i = if keep i then v i else 0 := by
findings.problem:
`coordinateProjection` is an opaque `def` built from `matrixOperator (Matrix.diagonal …)`, and the file provides no simp lemma for its coordinates. Plain `simp` therefore cannot reduce `coordinateProjection keep v i` to its natural normal form, `if keep i then v i else 0` (or to `v i` / `0` once `keep i` is decided).

Every caller has to supply the lemma by hand:
- ProjectedGraphTesting, line 34: `simp [coordinateProjection_apply, paddingTestVector, hq]`.
- ProjectedLiouvilleVector, line 20: `simp [coordinateProjection_apply, …]`.
- PrimeComplexMatrix, line 78: the same.
- This file, line 37: `simp only [coordinateProjection_apply]`.

When `¬ keep i` is known, callers also have to add `ite_eq_right` by hand: line 44 here (`rw [coordinateProjection_apply, ite_eq_right hkeep]`) and ProjectedGraphTesting line 31 (`simp only [coordinateProjection_apply, ite_eq_right hk]`). The file gives no canonical rule for the decided cases.
findings.proposed_change:
Mark the coordinate formula as a simp lemma: `@[simp] lemma coordinateProjection_apply …`. The RHS no longer mentions `coordinateProjection`, so it cannot loop. This matches Mathlib's `@[simp] Finsupp.indicator_apply`, which also has an `if` on the right.

Also add (or use instead, if the `if` form is not wanted in the global simp set) the decided-case simp lemmas, following the `Set.indicator_of_mem` / `indicator_of_notMem` pattern:
```lean
@[simp] lemma coordinateProjection_apply_of_keep {keep : V → Prop} (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ V) {i : V} (h : keep i) :
    coordinateProjection keep v i = v i := by simp [coordinateProjection_apply, h]
@[simp] lemma coordinateProjection_apply_of_not_keep {keep : V → Prop} (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ V) {i : V} (h : ¬ keep i) :
    coordinateProjection keep v i = 0 := by simp [coordinateProjection_apply, h]
```
Line 44 could then be `rw [coordinateProjection_apply_of_not_keep _ hkeep] at he`, and ProjectedGraphTesting line 31 could be `simp [hk]`.
findings.benefit: `simp [hp, hq, …]` would reduce projected coordinates without users having to remember to pass `coordinateProjection_apply`. The `ite_eq_right` boilerplate in the `¬ keep i` case would go away. The projection would then have the same coordinate-level simp normal form that `matrixOperator_apply` already gives the underlying operator, and the four-plus downstream call sites would get shorter and less fragile.

evidence.excerpt: @[simp] lemma matrixOperator_apply (A : ι → ι → ℂ) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (i : ι) :
theorem indicator_apply [DecidableEq ι] : indicator s f i = if hi : i ∈ s then f i hi else 0 := by
